prompt_md: Bites come completely at random (no rhythm, no memory), one per 30 minutes on average. You've had none for 20 minutes. Average further wait for a bite, in minutes?
prompt_short: Random bites, one per 30 min on average. None for 20 min. Further wait?
hint_md: Do the fish know how long you have waited?
explain_intuition_md: With truly random bites, the last 20 minutes tell the fish nothing; the clock effectively restarts. So the expected wait is still the full 30 minutes. Subtracting 20 from 30 treats bites like a timer that is due to go off.
explain_math_md: Waits in a Poisson process are exponential and memoryless: $$P(T > 20 + s \mid T > 20) = P(T > s) \Rightarrow E[T - 20 \mid T > 20] = E[T] = 30$$
